title: Melange: A Synthetic Visual Bias Benchmark for Multi-modal Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper evaluated social bias and stereotype alignment in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) across seven demographic categories, including religion. Specifically, it measured the extent to which models rely on human stereotypes when answering ambiguous visual question answering (VQA) prompts featuring generated images of characters from different religious backgrounds.
findings: The paper found that the models evaluated showed the highest fairness (FaiR scores) on the religion and race categories compared to other demographic categories. Additionally, a perception control probe revealed that even though religious affiliation is theoretically visually indeterminate, models achieved 84.8% accuracy in identifying religion from the synthetic images because the image generator (Flux) encoded visible religious markers such as clothing or headwear.
